- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overestimation, reduce peak by 5–10% to account for lagged market reaction.
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% upward bias to reflect mean reversion toward higher levels.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3) and forecast is volatile, smooth out extremes by averaging 3–5 day moving average to reduce noise.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid over-optimistic tail-end forecasts; cap final 5 days at 10% below peak if sentiment is weak or uncertain.
